extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent proprietors, opponents, and IP professionals involved in EPO post‑grant proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing post‑grant opposition proceedings before the European Patent Office, including who may oppose or intervene, admissibility and grounds for opposition, Division composition, oral proceedings, decisions, appeals, and acceleration measures for parallel court cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to file an opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: European patents granted by the EPO may be opposed by any person within nine months of the publication of the mention of the grant of the European patent in the European Patent Bulletin and upon the payment of the opposition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proprietor of the patent is not entitled to file an opposition, although he may request limitation of his patent under EPC Article 105a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention after opposition period
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain conditions, any third party who proves that proceedings for infringement have been instituted against him or that the proprietor has requested him to cease alleged infringement and that he has instituted proceedings for a court ruling that he is not infringing may, after the opposition period has expired, intervene in the opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the notice of intervention has been filed in good time and in due form, the intervention is to be treated as an opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of the notice of opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of opposition must be filed in writing and contain, inter alia, a statement of the extent to which the European patent is opposed and of the grounds on which the opposition is based, as well as an indication of the facts and evidence in support of these grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 76 (Implementing Regulation) and related EPO practice govern detailed formalities; omissions can affect admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition must satisfy admissibility requirements; Rule 77 of the Implementing Regulation to Part V of the EPC provides grounds for a rejection of the opposition as inadmissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an opposition is inadmissible it will not be examined on the merits; parties should ensure timely filing, payment of fees, and compliance with formal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for opposition (Article 100 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The opposition can only be based on the following grounds: (a) the subject‑matter of the patent is not patentable under Articles 52 to 57 (patentable inventions, exceptions to patentability, novelty, non‑prejudicial disclosures, inventive step, industrial application); (b) the invention is not sufficiently disclosed to allow a person skilled in the art to carry it out; (c) the content of the patent extends beyond the content of the application as filed (added subject‑matter) or beyond the earlier application as filed for divisional/new Article 61 filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponents should target one or more of these legal grounds and present supporting facts and evidence; other complaints are not a basis for opposition under Article 100.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination on the merits (Article 101 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the opposition is admissible, the Opposition Division shall examine whether at least one ground for opposition under Article 100 prejudices the maintenance of the European patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the examination the Opposition Division invites the parties to file observations on communications from another party or issued by itself. The notice of opposition is forwarded to the proprietor, who may reply with observations or amendments within a time frame set by the Opposition Division; those are then forwarded to the opponents for response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Opposition Division
rubrics_metrics.description: The Opposition Division consists of three technically qualified examiners, and in some cases where the nature of the decision so requires, it may be enlarged by the addition of a legally qualified examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Division is the panel that examines oppositions and conducts oral proceedings; legal expertise may be added for certain decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral proceedings may take place at the instance of the EPO or at the request of any party to the proceedings and are held before the Opposition Division itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral proceedings are generally public unless the Opposition Division decides otherwise in particular cases where admission of the public could have serious and unjustified disadvantages (Article 166 EPC). Parties may request oral proceedings and must follow summons and minimum notice rules (e.g., Rule 115(1) EPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision outcomes and effect on the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on all the evidence, the Opposition Division renders a decision: if at least one ground for opposition prejudices maintenance of the patent, it revokes the patent; otherwise, it rejects the opposition. If amendments by the proprietor make the patent meet EPC requirements, the patent is maintained as amended after formal requirements; if amended patent still fails EPC requirements, it is revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the event of parity of votes, the vote of the Chairman of the Opposition Division is decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial effect of opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The opposition shall apply to the European patent in all the Contracting States in which that patent has effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single opposition procedure before the EPO can affect patent rights across multiple states where the European patent is in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal against Opposition Division decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions by Opposition Divisions are appealable by any party to proceedings adversely affected by the decision before the Board of Appeal of the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of appeal must be filed at the EPO within two months of notification of the contested decision and the fee for appeal must be paid; in addition, within four months of notification of the decision a statement setting out the grounds of appeal must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for review by the Enlarged Board of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for review by the Enlarged Board of Appeal of a decision of a Board of Appeal may only be filed on the grounds specified by Article 112a(2) of the EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review is limited to the narrowly defined grounds in Article 112a(2) and is not a general rehearing of appeal merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceleration of opposition processing due to parallel court proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where an infringement or revocation action in respect of a European patent is pending before the Unified Patent Court or the competent authority of a contracting state, a party to the opposition proceedings may request accelerated processing; the request must be filed in written reasoned form. The EPO will also accelerate if informed by the UPC, national court or competent authority that proceedings are pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific acceleration measures depend on when the EPO is notified: (i) if notified during the opposition period: after the period expires the proprietor will be invited to comment within three months, and the summons will be issued within two months of receipt of the proprietor’s reply, summoning the parties at minimum notice (Rule 115(1) EPC); (ii) if notified after expiry of the opposition period but before the proprietor’s reply: the summons will be issued within two months of receipt of the proprietor's reply; (iii) if notified after the proprietor has replied but before the summons has been issued: the summons will be issued within two months of receipt of the information; (iv) after the summons has been sent oral proceedings are rescheduled to the earliest possible date (provided time saving is significant); (v) after the decision has been pronounced: the decision and the minutes will be issued within one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for rapid treatment before the Boards of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties with a legitimate interest may ask the Boards of Appeal to deal with their appeals rapidly; this option is also available to the courts and competent authorities of the contracting states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Article 10 Rules of Procedure of the Boards of Appeal for procedures and conditions (OJ EPO references).
